artikel.titel: FX Daily: Dollar rally needs more risk-off fuel
artikel.text: Contagion from AI to defensive stocks in the US and worldwide allowed the dollar to rally even before the strong US jobs market report. But unless risk sentiment remains poor this week, lower front-end US rates should favour a weaker dollar, even if inflation tomorrow comes in slightly hotter than expected

artikel.titel: China’s inflation cooled in October amid falling food prices
artikel.text: ASIA/PACIFIC: China’s inflation moderated as food costs matched a 13-month low, driven by a sharp decline in vegetable prices. Core inflation dipped to a 9-month low of 0.8%. China has emerged from deflation this year, helped by firmer energy and technology prices, but inflation remains well below target

artikel.titel: Robust US jobs market boosts December rate hike chances
artikel.text: NORTH AMERICA: The Federal Reserve has been focusing more on inflation recently, but a strong jobs report for October makes a December rate hike an even easier decision

artikel.titel: More signs of life in Hungary’s economy
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: Both industry and retail sales expanded in September. Positive surprises appeared in both sets of data. As Hungary’s growth is expected to be supported by internal factors, the external influence remains the only question mark in the recovery story

artikel.titel: CEE & CCA week ahead: Polish GDP and regional inflation data
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: Poland will release third-quarter GDP, final inflation and current account data next week, while Hungary publishes September inflation figures

artikel.titel: THINK Ahead: Markets get a fright, but central banks won’t spook that easily
artikel.text: Tumbling oil prices and a brutal sell-off in tech stocks are making investors think twice about the direction of interest rates. But even after a roller coaster week, James Smith argues central banks will take more convincing

artikel.titel: FX Daily: Tech collapses, FX shrugs
artikel.text: A delayed reaction to the Democrat blue wave has seen some powerful selling of tech stocks. A little surprisingly, the reaction in FX markets has remained very muted. FX participants so far see this as an idiosyncratic re-pricing of the tech sector, rather than a harbinger of recession. Expect defensive FX to outperform, rather than a broad dollar decline

artikel.titel: Asia week ahead: Philippine GDP and key data on China, Taiwan, and Japan
artikel.text: ASIA/PACIFIC: Philippine GDP is the highlight of the week, alongside China’s inflation and trade data, Taiwan’s trade figures, and Japan’s household spending and price indicators

artikel.titel: German industry defies higher energy prices and low water levels – for now
artikel.text: EUROPE: Activity in the automotive and construction sectors experienced a post-holiday surge in September, adding to the resilience of German industry

artikel.titel: Rates Spark: Treasury heat from tech flight - but for how long?
artikel.text: A creeping move lower in equities would eventually be ignored by Treasuries. But a large dump in equities would not. Treasuries are so far very much in vogue. In Europe, bond spreads are widening again as we head into another weekend of street unrest. Friday sees US jobs data competing for the spotlight, although Thursday's low claims were broadly ignored
